doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Coltrane, going out, and accessibility
summary: He wants to know where the band is and be challenging but accessible.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Speaking of that. Are you a fan of the Coltrane type music and that era where people played on and on and on?

When John Coltrane played out, at least I know where he is. Some people play out and I don’t know where they are. You know. I’m not a fan of out. A little bit out, but I want to hear the song, or I want to hear a reference to a song. I want to know where the band is, where everybody is. For those who haven’t heard it, when Coltrane said to Miles, or Miles said to Coltrane, “listen man, you’ve got to stop playing those 45 minute solos. People are walking out.” And Coltrane says, “well I finish a chorus and I come up with another idea, so I want to play that idea, and when I finish that idea I thought I left this out or I got another idea and I want to play that. I don’t know how to stop.” And Miles said, “just take the horn out your mouth.” You know? So I think anyway you have to realize that you are performing for an audience. I mean some people want to come and see you go off into oblivion. And some people don’t. Especially if you’re a singer anyway. I want to be challenging but accessible. I want people to get it. I don’t want people to go out and go, “what happened in there?” I want them to hear it. Even if it’s something that they never heard before. I want to walk out, if I go listen to someone, I want to walk out humming something. I want to hear some kind of something.
